name: Francis Bach
body:
Thanks, Pierre, for sharing your insightful and optimistic views. I particularly value the need to keep "pleasure and serendipity at the core of the scientific endeavour", and I like how AI should "increase the marginal return of an additional researcher instead of decreasing it". This reinforces the importance of training the new generations of these researchers. 

I am sure infinitely many weather or sailing metaphors have been proposed for this new research environment that AI is bringing upon us. Let me propose my own (sorry it only works for skiers): we are currently within a huge snowstorm of a never-before-seen kind, with ahead of us the need to ski on a different and new type of snow. Very much like "powder", it will require a different set of skiing skills; we will also have our series of falls, but once we master it, this will hopefully be unusually rewarding, and we will never want to ski on old snow anymore.
